## Summary

Under the supplied SEBI text, designated persons and their immediate relatives must not trade in securities when the trading window is closed.

The trading window is closed when the compliance officer determines that a designated person or class of designated persons can reasonably be expected to possess unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI). The closure applies to the securities to which that UPSI relates. The supplied text also states that, for UPSI not originating within the listed company, the trading window may not be closed.

Around financial results, the trading restriction period applies:

- From the end of every quarter; and
- Until 48 hours after the declaration of the financial results.

Thus, the specified restriction period is from quarter-end through 48 hours after results are declared. Certain prescribed transactions and bona fide pledges may be excluded, subject to applicable pre-clearance and other requirements.

## Relevant quotation

> “The trading window shall be closed when the compliance officer determines that a designated person or class of designated persons can reasonably be expected to have possession of unpublished price sensitive information.”

> “Designated persons and their immediate relatives shall not trade in securities when the trading window is closed.”

> “Trading restriction period shall be made applicable from the end of every quarter till 48 hours after the declaration of financial results.”

Source: supplied evidence, E2, page 61.

## Summary

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, **“tax year” means the twelve-month period of the financial year beginning on 1 April and ending on 31 March**.

For a newly started business or profession, or a newly arising source of income, the first tax year begins on:

- the date the business or profession is set up; or
- the date the new source of income comes into existence,

and ends on the following 31 March.

For example, if a business is set up on 1 October 2026, its first tax year would run from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.

The Act is stated in the supplied material to come into force on 1 April 2026. Legal currentness and the cited material have not been independently verified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

> “For the purposes of this Act, ‘tax year’ means the twelve months period of the financial year commencing on the 1st April.”

> “In the case of a business or profession newly set up, or a source of income newly coming into existence in any financial year, the tax year shall be the period beginning with” the relevant setup or commencement date “and ending with the said financial year.”

## Summary

Under section 16 of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person must generally satisfy these conditions before claiming input tax credit (ITC):

- The goods or services must be used, or intended to be used, in the course or furtherance of business.
- The person must possess:
  - a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under the CGST Act, or
  - another prescribed tax-paying document.
- The invoice or debit-note details must have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient.
- The registered person must have received the goods or services.
- The credit must be taken subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions and in the manner specified under section 49.
- Under section 41, eligible ITC is self-assessed in the return and credited provisionally to the electronic credit ledger.

Receipt may be deemed to occur in specified cases, such as delivery to the recipient or another person on the registered person’s direction, or services supplied to a person on the registered person’s direction and account.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

Section 16(1) states that ITC is available for supplies “which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business.”

Section 16(2) provides that no ITC is available unless the registered person:

> “is in possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under this Act”

and

> “he has received the goods or services or both.”

The evidence also includes the requirement that invoice or debit-note details must be furnished by the supplier and communicated to the recipient.

cases.answer:
## Summary

Under section 16 of the CGST Act, a registered person must satisfy these conditions before taking input tax credit:

- The goods or services must be used, or intended to be used, in the course or furtherance of business.
- The person must possess:
  - A tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under the Act, or another prescribed tax-paying document.
  - Invoice or debit-note details furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient, as specified under section 37.
- The registered person must have received the goods or services. Receipt may be deemed where:
  - Goods are delivered to the recipient or another person on the registered person’s direction; or
  - Services are provided to a person on the registered person’s direction and account.
- The credit must be taken subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions and in the manner specified under section 49.
- Under section 41, eligible input tax credit is self-assessed in the return and credited provisionally to the electronic credit ledger. It may be utilised only for payment of self-assessed output tax as stated in the return.

Legal currentness is unverified because the supplied text is stated to be amended up to 1 January 2022. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

Section 16(2) states that no registered person is entitled to input tax credit unless:

> “(a) he is in possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under this Act, or such other tax paying documents as may be prescribed;”

> “(aa) the details of the invoice or debit note referred to in clause (a) has been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and such details have been communicated to the recipient…”

> “(b) he has received the goods or services or both.”
